transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I just can’t seem to get a full night’s sleep anymore, my mind won’t let me rest and I wake up feeling exhausted. It has gotten to the point where I feel completely drained during the day, and I really need some help figuring out how to get some rest.
Aside from your sleep troubles, do you find yourself constantly worrying or feeling anxious about various everyday things throughout the day?

Yes, my mind is constantly scanning for things that could go wrong, like my mother's health or a server crashing at work. Even a missed call or an email sets off these worst-case scenarios, and no matter how much I tell myself to stop, the looping worries just won't let me focus on anything.
Along with the anxiety and sleep issues, have you also been feeling down, depressed, or losing interest in activities you normally enjoy?

I wouldn't say I feel deeply depressed, but I have definitely lost the ability to enjoy the things I used to love. I’ve had to pull back from my Saturday walking club, church activities, and even crocheting because I just feel too exhausted and distracted by my worries to focus on them anymore.
How long have you been experiencing these constant worries and sleep difficulties? Has it been going on for more or less than six months?

It has definitely been much longer than six months. This constant worrying and lack of sleep has been building up for about a year now, starting around the time my mother's health crises began ramping up.
Even though you mentioned not feeling deeply depressed, have you been experiencing a persistent feeling of sadness, emptiness, or low mood most of the day, nearly every day?
No, I don't really feel a persistent sense of sadness or emptiness. It is more that I feel constantly anxious, overwhelmed, and physically exhausted from the continuous worry and my lack of sleep.
Along with the worry and fatigue, have you been experiencing physical symptoms like muscle tension, trembling, or feeling constantly keyed up and on edge?

Yes, I feel wound tight all the time, like my body is constantly bracing for some emergency call. I find myself pacing in the kitchen or tapping my foot during meetings, and my muscles are so tense that I can't even sit still to enjoy my crochet anymore.
Do you also experience physical reactions like a racing heart, sweating, dry mouth, or stomach upset when you feel particularly anxious?

No, I don't really experience those kinds of symptoms like a racing heart, sweating, or an upset stomach. It's more that my body just feels incredibly tense, wound tight, and physically on edge all the time.
Have you found yourself feeling more irritable, snappy, or easily annoyed with others lately because of all this stress and lack of sleep?

Yes, I have been feeling much more irritable and snappy lately. I find myself snapping at my husband over tiny things like misplacing the remote, and at my brother when he's just a few minutes late to help with my mom. I feel terrible and guilty afterward because they don't deserve it, but I'm just so exhausted and on edge all the time.
Are you currently taking any medications, or do you have any medical conditions like thyroid problems that could be contributing to these symptoms?
No, I am not currently taking any regular medications. I also don't have any known medical conditions like thyroid issues, as far as I know.
Do you regularly consume caffeine, alcohol, or use any other substances to help cope with your anxiety or sleep issues?
I don't use alcohol or any other substances to help me cope with my anxiety or sleep issues. I do drink my usual cup of coffee in the morning, but that is about it.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets all diagnostic criteria for Generalized Anxiety Disorder (ICD-10 F41.1). She presents with excessive, uncontrollable worry regarding multiple everyday domains (mother's health, work) persisting for approximately one year (well over the 6-month threshold). This anxiety is accompanied by prominent somatic and psychological symptoms, including marked muscle tension, restlessness, physical fatigue, irritability, concentration difficulties due to looping worries, and severe sleep disturbance. Major depressive disorder, substance-induced anxiety, and general medical conditions (such as thyroid dysfunction) have been ruled out. The symptoms cause significant functional impairment, leading to withdrawal from social and recreational activities.
